announcement: Independent 3D texturing · Windows x64 development preview
heroTitle:
Layers when you paint.
*Procedural when you need it.*
heroLede: Paint with layers. Build with nodes. Keep both in one material workflow.
heroNote: One material. Two connected ways to create.
introTitle:
One workspace.
*Two connected ways to work.*
introBody: Paint and build materials with layers, then open the graph to shape and reuse the procedural logic behind them. Baking, UV checks and material review stay part of the same asset workflow.
donateTitle: Made by one developer, for artists
donateBody: Surface3D is a solo project built around a simple goal: give artists an open, approachable alternative to expensive texturing tools. Support helps fund development time, testing, documentation and distribution.

news.title: Texture work, kept in flow
news.body: Paint on the model, work with clear layers, and open the graph whenever you want deeper control.

news.title: Build a surface once
news.body: Shape procedural details into reusable outputs for the materials and layers in your project.

news.title: A tool growing with artists
news.body: Surface3D is evolving around practical texturing workflows, clear controls, and reliable output.

features.title: Layer-based materials
features.body: Build a surface with fill layers, painted details, masks and folders, while keeping each part editable.
features.points:
Fill and paint layers
Masks, blend modes and channel opacity
Folders and pass-through composition

features.title: Teach masks
features.body: Paint where an effect should go and where it should not. Surface3D learns the rule and fills the whole model.
features.points:
Left: here, right: not here, with a live mask
Learns 25 things: edges, cavities, water flow, metal, wood grain…
Readable rule you can adjust with sliders
Grunge look learned from how you paint

features.title: Physical weathering
features.body: Rust, moss, dirt, dust and leak stains computed from how they form on this model: rain, sky, edges and gravity.
features.points:
Five templates, no bakes needed
Age, amount and climate controls
"See why" shows the measurement behind it

features.title: Sculpting
features.body: Dent, fold, carve and inflate the surface in a live Sculpt layer. Smart masks and edge damage follow your sculpt.
features.points:
Clay, crease, pinch, flatten, scrape and more
Height and normal detail in one undo step
Bake + Sculpt for masks that react to it

features.title: Edge damage
features.body: Chips and dents along real mesh edges and bevels, baked into the normal map and updated live.
features.points:
Works on bevels and real meshes
Pick which edges get damaged
Feeds smart masks like a high-poly bake

features.title: Brush engine and paint tools
features.body: A full painting toolset with 2K and 4K layers that stay responsive.
features.points:
Brush, eraser, smudge, clone, fill, mask brush, decals
Pen pressure, symmetry, smoothing, stencils
Splines and particles on the model

features.title: Procedural materials, connected to your layers
features.body: Use a graph for the parts that benefit from procedural control, then combine the result with your painted material.
features.points:
Connect generators, maps and filters
Reuse results with live anchors
Mix hand-painted and procedural detail

features.title: Tileable materials from photographs
features.body: Turn a photograph into a starting point for a repeating material, then refine the seams and surface channels.
features.points:
Offset and tileability tools
Seam cleanup with paint and cloning
Create and adjust material maps
features.statusDetail: Results depend on the source photo and cleanup.

features.title: Tileable patterns
features.body: Build repeating surfaces with shapes, noises, samplers and splatters.
features.points:
Tiles, repeated shapes and distributions
Control scale, rotation and variation
Combine patterns into reusable materials

features.title: High-poly to low-poly baking
features.body: Transfer surface detail from a detailed model onto the mesh you want to texture.
features.points:
Low/high mesh setup and projection cages
Normal, occlusion and curvature maps
Selective mesh-map baking
features.statusDetail: Engine availability depends on your hardware.

features.title: Vertex colors in materials
features.body: Use color data stored on your mesh to drive masks, material variation and procedural effects.
features.points:
Read mesh vertex-color data
Use channels to guide a mask
Combine vertex colors with textures and graphs
features.statusDetail: Requires a mesh containing vertex colors.

features.title: Paint inside a graph
features.body: Add hand-authored marks and cleanup directly into a procedural texture workflow.
features.points:
Paint-node results
Clone-based texture cleanup
Combine strokes with filters and generators

features.title: Stencil-guided painting
features.body: Use a camera-facing texture overlay to place and paint details with more control.
features.points:
Image stencil and opacity
Placement controls
Levels and inversion

features.title: UVs and projection
features.body: A dedicated UV workspace: inspect islands, unwrap, and pack them tightly so less texture is wasted.
features.points:
UV inspection, unwrap and transform
Smarter automatic packing
Triplanar and other projection modes

features.title: Reusable materials and texture outputs
features.body: Keep useful results in your library and share graph outputs between parts of a project.
features.points:
Named live texture outputs
Material and graph assets
Reusable masks and patterns

features.title: Export for your 3D workflow
features.body: Take your finished texture maps into any 3D software that supports standard PBR textures.
features.points:
Export selected texture channels
Choose output resolution
Keep color and data maps distinct

features.title: Material review
features.body: Review your asset with lighting and camera controls before exporting it.
features.points:
HDRI environments
Turntable review
Post-processing controls

features.title: Faster high-resolution iteration
features.body: Reduce pauses when editing layers and complex graphs at higher texture resolutions.
features.points:
Smarter result reuse
More targeted updates
Ongoing CPU and GPU optimization
features.statusDetail: 2K and 4K painting is fast since 0.48; work on large graphs continues.

features.title: A broader artist asset library
features.body: Grow the collection of editable patterns, masks, filters and material starting points.
features.points:
Organized by practical use
Exposed controls
Ready to use in layers or graphs
features.statusDetail: Future additions; no release date is promised.

tutorials.body: A video walkthrough of building a pattern and reusing its graph output.

homepage.layerBody: Build materials with fills, paint, masks and effects.
homepage.graphBody: Connect textures, mesh maps and generators. Reuse the result in your layers.
homepage.bakeBody: Capture surface detail from your mesh. Check normals, curvature and occlusion directly on the object.
homepage.uvBody: Inspect your islands, make a quick transform, unwrap and pack. Keep texture placement clear before the final material pass.
homepage.renderBody: Check your materials under HDRI lighting. Export standard PBR maps for your 3D workflow.
homepage.aboutTitle: One developer. A connected material workspace.
homepage.aboutGoal: Make capable 3D texturing accessible to every artist: familiar layers when you paint, procedural control when you need it, and smart tools that understand the model.
homepage.aboutBuild: A native Windows application with its own GPU renderer, so painting, sculpting and masks stay fast at 2K and 4K.
homepage.aboutDevelopment: Surface3D is developed independently, with frequent releases shaped by artist feedback on Discord. Every release is listed with its changes on GitHub.
homepage.aboutExperience: Surface3D grew out of my own work texturing environments and props. It brings together the tools and workflows I wanted while making those assets.
homepage.aboutAI: Surface3D is built with the help of AI agents. I guide the product using my experience in 3D environment and prop texturing; AI agents help write, debug and improve the code. If you prefer not to use or support software built with AI agents, please take that into account before downloading or supporting the project.
homepage.aboutOriginality: Surface3D is an original, independently developed project. It is not decompiled or reverse-engineered software, and it is not a clone. It brings layer-based painting and procedural material creation together in a new workflow.
homepage.aboutIntro: A native texturing app for painting, sculpting, smart weathering and procedural materials, made by a 3D artist for artists. Free for Windows.
